A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

optic ataxia can be viewed as a disorder of the global tuning field, and that this disorder is a direct consequence of the breakdown in the cortico-corticocortical systems linking the parietal and premotor cortices.
optic ataxia, as a disorder of the visuomotor transformation, is the consequence of a breakdown of the global coding properties of parietal neurons.

optic ataxia results from the breakdown of the distributed networks linking parietal to the premotor cortex, which are essential for the composition and the execution of visually guided eye- and hand-movements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
optic ataxia, as well as many other forms of parietal neglect, is not a disorder of perception, but a disorder of motor planning and execution.
